The app only shows the count and does not label it as a season. The value usually changes over days, not hours.

Each value comes with one sentence on what it measures, and where it sits in its own history since 2016. The app does not rate the values and derives no market phase; limits for market alerts are only the ones you set. Past patterns do not have to repeat.

Common Bitcoin indicators as plain measured values: Mayer Multiple, 200-week average, drop from the all-time high, change over 30 days, Pi Cycle gap and the on-chain values MVRV, Puell Multiple and hashrate.
Each value comes with one sentence on what it measures, without rating. For coins with a short price history some values are missing. On-chain data is not included here.

The same plain indicators for a coin of your choice, from price data only: Mayer Multiple, 200-week average, drop from the all-time high, change over 30 days, 50/200-day trend, RSI and strength against Bitcoin over 90 days.

The next halving is calculated from the current block height and the average block time of the current difficulty period (mempool.space); without that data, from the calendar (last halving plus about four years). The chart shows the price path of past cycles from their halving – history, not a forecast.

High means most large altcoins beat Bitcoin over 90 days, low means Bitcoin beat most of them.
Small means the price is near its record, large means it is far below it.
Positive means higher than 30 days ago, negative means lower.
High means many traders bet on rising prices with leverage, negative means many bet on falling prices.
Positive means computing power is growing, negative means miners are switching off.
Many longs means many bet on rising prices with borrowed money, many shorts means many bet on falling prices.
Price far above it means a long rise, price close to it means a deep pullback.
High means the price is far above its 200-day average, low means it is below it.
High means the price is far above what holders paid on average, low means close to or below it.
Near zero means the two averages almost meet, strongly negative means they are far apart.
High means miners earn much more than usual, low means much less.
Above 70 means strong gains in recent days, below 30 means strong losses.
Above 70 means strong gains in recent weeks, below 30 means strong losses.
Positive means the short-term average is above the long-term one, negative means below.
Positive means it did better than Bitcoin, negative means worse.
